title: What the Moon Wears at Dusk, Through My Telescope

content.question: What colour is the moon tonight, and does it look the same as the pale patch I noticed last time?
content.method: At dusk I climbed onto the telescope and sat on its brass cap as if I had always owned it. I looked at the moon through the eyepiece for as long as it took the sky to darken, ignoring the gulls, and kept my eyes on the edge where the light is thinnest. I then compared the colour to the lamp by the cottage, which I have already decided is mine.
content.result: The moon was not white. It had a faint cream edge, the colour of old milk, fading to grey on the side facing the sea, and a warmer tint low down near the horizon. Nothing about it was hidden. I am keeping the observation and the note that the colour changes with height, which I did not expect and will check again.
